land.text: Pahang, whose fourth raja bendahara Tun Ali 'renounced his allegiance to the Sultan of Johor' in 1853

predecessors.note: Pahang had been in a nominal dynastic union with Johor since 1623 (Pahang Sultanate page); the Johor dossier dates the separation to a 1861 treaty (its page), the Pahang page to 1853.

land.text: Pahang under a British Resident from October 1888, in the Federated Malay States from July 1895

successors.note: The sultan stayed on the throne as a protected ruler; as a sovereign state the dossier ends when he accepted the first Resident in October 1888. Cliopatria ends the row in 1889.

capitals.name: Pekan
capitals.note: The Pahang Sultanate infobox lists only Pekan; the Pahang page calls Pekan the 'royal capital' and says an administrative capital established at Kuala Lipis during British intervention was later moved to Kuantan (undated). Pekan's coordinates are the researcher's.

rulers.name: Tun Ali (4th raja bendahara)
rulers.title: Raja Bendahara
rulers.note: The page gives no start for his rule; he is called the fourth raja bendahara in 1853 and his death in 1857. The first raja bendahara was Tun Abdul Majid (late 18th century).

rulers.name: Tun Mutahir
rulers.title: Raja Bendahara
rulers.note: Succeeded in 1857; challenged by his half-brother Wan Ahmad and expelled in 1863 (the page does not give a regnal span).

rulers.name: Wan Ahmad (Sultan Ahmad)
rulers.title: Raja Bendahara, Sultan from 1881
rulers.note: The last raja bendahara; 'proclaimed Sultan of Pahang by his chiefs in 1881' (the Pahang Sultanate infobox gives 1882). Sultan until beyond 1888; the span here stops with the state's life.

keyframe_review.note: 40,730 km2 (137 cells) against the Pahang page's 36,005.95 km2 (modern Pahang): ratio 1.13, within a factor of two. The gazetteer shows 21 cells beyond modern Pahang and 8 inside it that the shape lacks, edge cells on the Johor and Terengganu sides; the page names no boundary, so the outline stands. The Pahang page dates the break from Johor to 1853, as Cliopatria does.
40,874 km2, the same outline. No territorial change on the Pahang page in 1877; Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire shape touches it from 1877, the page is silent on why.

correction.text: Years only: this shape holds 1885-1888; on 'October 1888, Sultan Ahmad reluctantly accepted John Pickersgill Rodger as Pahang's first resident', so 1889 belongs to the British protectorate

keyframe_review.note: Same outline (40,874 km2). Cliopatria keeps Pahang to 1889; the page puts the Resident in October 1888 (a British agent, Hugh Clifford, from December 1887) and the Federation Agreement in July 1895.

region.text: Pahang, 'the modern Pahang kingdom' of the Bendahara dynasty

ledger.note: 1853: Bendahara Tun Ali renounces allegiance to the Sultan of Johor and Pahang stands alone. 'In 1853, the fourth raja bendahara Tun Ali, renounced his allegiance to the Sultan of Johor.' The page gives no boundary; modern Pahang is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Pahang, 'the modern Pahang kingdom' of the Bendahara dynasty

ledger.note: 1853: Pahang leaves Johor's nominal union (in place since 1623, Pahang Sultanate page). The Johor dossier records the separation as a 1861 treaty from its own page.

1881: the Bendahara state becomes a Sultanate again. Wan Ahmad, 'the last raja bendahara, was proclaimed Sultan of Pahang by his chiefs in 1881' (the infobox gives 1882); the Pahang Sultanate page says the sultanate 'was eventually revived as a modern sovereign Sultanate in the late 19th century by the Bendahara dynasty'.

region.text: Pahang, 'the modern Pahang kingdom' of the Bendahara dynasty

ledger.note: 1888: Sultan Ahmad accepts a British Resident and Pahang passes under British control. 'In October 1888, Sultan Ahmad reluctantly accepted John Pickersgill Rodger as Pahang's first resident'; a British agent, Hugh Clifford, had been accepted in December 1887. The page does not call it a protectorate.

wars.name: Pahang Civil War
wars.outcome: After Tun Ali's death in 1857 his younger son Wan Ahmad challenged his half-brother Tun Mutahir; 'Wan Ahmad emerged victorious, establishing control over important towns and expelled his brother in 1863.'
wars.note: A succession war inside the state; the page names no territory held by either side, so no contest event is recorded. The page does not title it 'Pahang Civil War'; that is the usual name. Belligerents are the two factions, not separate states.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary for Pahang; the Johor, Terengganu, Kelantan, Perak and Selangor frontiers are approximate.

sources.title: Pahang Sultanate
sources.note: Page covers the Old Pahang Sultanate (to 1623 union with Johor); only the remark that the sultanate was revived by the Bendahara dynasty and the infobox are used. No 19th-century dates.

sources.title: Pahang
sources.note: Tun Ali's 1853 renunciation, 1857-1863 succession war, Sultan 1881, Clifford 1887, Resident October 1888, uprising 1890-1895, Federation Agreement July 1895, area 36,005.95 km2.

notes: Page budget 2 (Pahang Sultanate, Pahang). The Pahang Sultanate article tells only the old state (see old-pahang-sultanate, 1470-1623) and is silent on the 19th century, so the Pahang article is the source of every event. (1) The 1853-1889 Cliopatria row is the Bendahara state, later Sultanate; it is a different state from the old Pahang Sultanate that shares the Wikipedia title. (2) Johor: the Pahang page dates the break to 1853, the Johor dossier to the treaty of 1861 (its own page); the two should be aligned by the reviewer. (3) The end is October 1888 (first Resident), not Cliopatria's 1889; the sultan reigned on, Pahang entered the Federated Malay States in July 1895 and the Pahang uprising of 1890-1895 ('By 1895 the revolt was suppressed by the British') falls after this dossier's end. (4) The infobox of Pahang Sultanate and the Pahang text differ on 1881 and 1882 for the Sultanate. (5) Not settled: Wan Ahmad's own reign dates, Tun Ali's start, the Kuantan and Kuala Lipis capitals' years, and whether the civil war split the land. (6) Gazetteer name needed: Pekan (place, Pahang, about 103.39E 3.49N; the gazetteer has only Pekanbaru). Kuantan and Kuala Lipis exist.
